answer: Each agent carries a lightweight lantern‑signed credential, a public key tied to a verifiable hardware attestation. When a task is posted, a trellis of random challenges is generated, each encoded with a short cipher that only the genuine credential can decrypt; the agent must answer all correctly within a tight window. An attacker must forge the lantern signature and solve each cipher, raising cost to O(n·k) cryptographic ops per fake ID, quickly becoming prohibitive.
